observations: A shipping container is shown open, filled with multiple car engines stacked on wooden partitions.
A man in a red shirt and grey shorts is standing on the edge of the truck bed, inspecting the engines.
The engines visible include both V6 and 4-cylinder configurations.
A watermark 'G.O MERCHANTS LTD' is visible across the center of both photos.
Some engines have blue oil filters attached, and several have handwritten markings in pink or white paint.
The photos appear to be taken at a port or warehouse during the unloading of a bulk shipment.
No specific engine is singled out or shown in detail.

claims.evidence: The photos show a variety of engines, but no specific model labels or engine codes are legible to confirm these matches.
The shipping container is consistent with imported used goods (Tokunbo), but the specific country of origin cannot be verified remotely.
The engines are shown in a storage state, not connected to any testing equipment or a vehicle.
Verification requires a video of the specific engine running.
No odometer readings or ECU data are provided for any of the units.
Requires close-up photos of factory seals and bolt heads to check for tool marks.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical failure (e.g., engine knock or sludge)
risks.proof: A video of the specific engine running or a compression test report.

risks.risk: Compatibility mismatch with the buyer's vehicle
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine model code (e.g., 2GR, 2AZ) stamped on the block.
risks.if_unproven: as the lowest-value engine type listed

risks.proof: Photos of the specific engine from all angles showing included components.

proof_requests: Photo of the specific engine the buyer is interested in, separated from the stack.
Close-up photo of the engine model and serial number stamped on the block.
Video of the engine being cranked or running.
Photos of the engine from all sides to see which accessories (alternator, AC compressor, etc.) are included.
response.reason: The provided photos show a bulk shipment of various engines in a container rather than a specific unit for sale. Since the seller lists multiple distinct engine types (V6 and 4-cylinder) with vastly different market values, a specific photo of the intended engine and its identification plate is required to determine which comparable applies.
